chunks: And al-Fudayl ibn Yasar narrated, he said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying: 'I entered [Mecca] with an Umrah, so where do I terminate the Talbiyah?' He said: 'Opposite the pass of the people of Medina (Aqabat al-Madiniyyin).' I asked: 'Where is the pass of the people of Medina?' He said: 'Opposite the dyers (Qassarin).'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The way to reconcile these narrations is to apply the last narration to those who came specifically via the Medina route, for they terminate the Talbiyah at the pass of the people of Medina. And the narration in which he said he terminates the Talbiyah at Dhi Taww is applied to those who came via the Iraq route. And the narration that included terminating it while looking at the Ka'bah is applied to one who had left Mecca for the Umrah. And in this way, there is no contradiction or conflict between them.

And the narration we mentioned in the first chapter, that the Umrah pilgrim terminates the Talbiyah when entering the Haram, we apply it as permissible (optional). And these narrations, despite their differing states, are upon excellence and recommendation.

And when Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated these narrations, he applied them to choice (option), thinking they were contradictory. And according to what we explained, they are not contradictory. And if they were contradictory, the way he mentioned would still be correct.

key_terms.الاسْتِحْبَاب: Al-Istihbab: Recommendation or commendability in Islamic law
key_terms.التَّلْبِيَة: Talbiyah: The ritual proclamation 'Labbayk' recited during Hajj and Umrah
key_terms.الْجَوَاز: Al-Jawaz: Permissibility or optionality (as opposed to strict obligation)
key_terms.الْحَرَم: Al-Haram: The sacred precincts of Mecca
key_terms.الْمَدِينِيُّون: Al-Madiniyyun: The people of Medina, referring to pilgrims arriving via that route
key_terms.ذِي طُوًى: Dhi Taww: A specific location near Mecca, often associated with the Prophet's mosque
key_terms.عَقَبَة: Aqabah: A pass or high point, here referring to a specific location near Mecca

ai.seo_question: Where should a pilgrim terminate their Talbiyah during Umrah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves apparent contradictions in the narrations regarding the termination of Talbiyah by contextualizing them according to the pilgrim's entry route—specifically distinguishing between those arriving from Medina, Iraq, or exiting Mecca. This method of reconciliation (jam' bayn al-akhbar) demonstrates that the variations reflect geographical specifics rather than conflicting obligations, a view supported by Abu Ja'far al-Babawayh who interpreted these differences as indicating recommendation (istihbab) rather than strict necessity.
